rationales.1: The answer is the headline: three of nine trails open lands instantly in the first mobile viewport with the closure alert directly beneath it.
rationales.2: Every status carries its word and one stable rendering, but caution and closed share the same orange and differ only by outline versus fill, which slows the most safety-critical distinction at a glance.
rationales.3: No-report-on-file rows, the dotted no-data day, the flagged estimated snowpack with its offline sensor note, and the never-assumed-open footer make every gap explicit.
rationales.4: Answer, alert, worth-knowing, then all nine trails in decision order is sound, though the conditions digest sits ahead of the trail list and pushes it a viewport down on mobile.
rationales.5: The editorial typography is disciplined and quiet, but the desktop composition leaves a large empty band between the hero and the trail list.
rationales.6: Long names, the burn pair, and the unreported rows sit evenly, and both modes plus the reflowed two-column weather strip hold up without breakage.
rationales.7: Stating the day's answer as a newspaper-style headline is a one-sentence signature that the typography, the calm list, and the footer all reinforce, and it is true of a daily conditions service.
rationales.8: Mechanics stay a conventional scrolling list; the headline hero and the single-accent palette are the one or two deliberate breaks, held in the brand layer.
rationales.9: Worth knowing, no report on file, and never assumed open or closed read as owned, calm, factual language a competitor would have to rewrite.
rationales.10: A returning hiker gets the answer in one fixation each morning with nothing mandatory in the way.
